title: Can you use the open door?
lines: An open door offers little freedom if leaving would cost you everything.
Freedom and Its Price asks what makes a choice usable, and what responsibility can reasonably demand.
Its starting scene gives several people the same permission while their capacities and dependencies remain different.

title: The conditions behind a choice
lines: From there, the book moves through work, citizenship, care, and power inside choices that seem voluntary.
A right to resign and a realistic way to survive resignation are not the same protection.
Knowing another person's limits still leaves hard questions about what each of us owes the other.

title: Freedom among other people
lines: Choices that feel private turn out to depend on conditions people must build and protect together.
Begin at the doorway, and consider who can actually walk through it.
